_comment: PROVEN INSTRUMENTS — C2B Web Design.
One entry per verify/ script that has been PROVED to go RED. Read by
verify/run.mjs, which suppresses the pass verdict of any script not listed
here. Nothing is blocked; every script still runs.
WHY: the expensive instrument failures all failed toward a PASS.
q5-stutter.mjs read 0/3 CLEAN on a visible stall; one-context.mjs read 2/2
while a WebGL context was created per question; the reveal instrument
reported 0ms on a live freeze. A false alarm costs minutes and gets
investigated. A FALSE PASS GETS BELIEVED.
⚠ A FALSIFY FLAG IS NOT A RED RUN. 15 scripts have a falsification mode; a
mode is a capability, a run is evidence. Only a run that was actually
performed and recorded in project-intelligence/ belongs here.
THREE REQUIREMENTS, ALL MANDATORY — an entry missing ANY is treated as
unproven by run.mjs, exactly as if it were not listed at all:
1. "redRun"      — it was shown to go RED. It CAN fail.
2. "emptyInput"  — it was pointed at NOTHING and reported an ABSENCE.
3. "stability"   — it declares whether its SUBJECT moves run to run.
⚠⚠ WHY THE SECOND ONE EXISTS — INSTRUMENT DEFECT #12, THE QUIET ZERO.
A harness reported a zero. The zero read as a finding. It manufactured a
design decision out of nothing — and that decision is INVISIBLE AFTERWARDS,
because the thing avoided never gets tried again. A false pass gets
believed; A FALSE CONSTRAINT GETS DESIGNED AROUND.
⚠ A zero meaning 'I looked and saw nothing happen' and a zero meaning 'I
never measured anything' ARE THE SAME CHARACTERS ON SCREEN. Going red
proves an instrument can move. It does NOT prove the instrument was ever
looking at anything.
⚠ THIS CANNOT BE CHECKED IN run.mjs. The runner sees only output text and
an exit code, and those two zeros are textually identical. A textual
detector was tried once and failed: a classifier keyed on DRIFT/STALL
matched an ordinary measurement line, because those words are this
codebase's SUBJECT MATTER. So the gate goes on the PROOF, not the output.
WHAT QUALIFIES AS AN EMPTY-INPUT CONTROL: the script is pointed at
something that genuinely contains nothing, and it REPORTS THE ABSENCE —
'NO REVEAL FOUND', 'NOTHING RESOLVED', 'no samples'. A ZERO VALUE DOES NOT
QUALIFY. '0ms' from an empty crop is the exact defect, not the control.
WORKED EXAMPLE — reveal-stall.mjs, 2026-08-18. Its crop was moved to empty
sky (y=200), where nothing happens by construction. It reported 'NO REVEAL
FOUND' on all 8 runs. Had it reported 0ms there, it would have been
indistinguishable from a clean run on a real crop, and every future 0ms
would have been unfalsifiable.
TO ADD AN ENTRY: run the script against a build carrying a real or injected
defect, confirm it goes RED, revert the injection, confirm it goes green
again. THEN point it at nothing and confirm it says so. Write both runs up
in project-intelligence/ and add the entry with the records they came from.
Do not add a script on the strength of a summary sentence in another
document — the runs themselves must be recorded.
⚠⚠ WHY THE THIRD ONE EXISTS — A SINGLE RUN IS NOT A MEASUREMENT.
The Q5 freeze varies by hundreds of milliseconds on ONE build in ONE session
with nothing changed. Every prior figure in this project — 720ms, 400ms,
626ms, and the 13 August bisect's whole staircase — was a single run or three
cold samples, and that bisect now carries a NOT SAFE banner because of it.
⚠ SO A PASS FROM ONE SAMPLE OF A VARYING SUBJECT IS A FALSE PASS WITH A PROOF
ATTACHED. redRun and emptyInput both pass, the entry reads fully proven, and
the number underneath it is one draw from a distribution nobody characterised.
TWO VALUES, and an entry declaring NEITHER is unproven:
"varies"        — the quantity moves run to run. The entry MUST also carry
"observedSpread" (min, max, runs, date, build) recording
what was actually seen. run.mjs suppresses the verdict of
a "varies" script that reports FEWER THAN THREE SAMPLES.
"deterministic" — it does not move, with "why" in one line (e.g. it
compares a geometry against a value it was handed).
Runs once, unchanged.
⚠⚠ THE RULE IS ABOUT THE SAMPLE COUNT BEHIND THE NUMBER — NOT HOW MANY TIMES
THE COMMAND WAS TYPED. Recorded because the brief that created this rule got
it wrong: it said "run the script three times", written without knowing
reveal-stall.mjs ALREADY TAKES FIVE SAMPLES PER INVOCATION.
⚠ RE-INVOKING WOULD HAVE BEEN WORSE THAN WASTEFUL. Three invocations are
three separate batches, and reveal-stall.mjs REFUSES to merge across builds
internally — it aborts on a build-id change, because "runs across two builds
are not one distribution". A runner stitching three batches together would
have MANUFACTURED A WIDER SPREAD THAN THE SUBJECT ACTUALLY HAS, from output
text it cannot verify came from one build. It would also have cost ~15 films
per verdict, which is slow enough that people reach for the direct route the
front door exists to close.
⚠ THREE IS ARBITRARY AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT PER-ENTRY. It is not derived —
it is the smallest count that can show a spread at all. A per-entry minimum
would invite arguing that an expensive script deserves fewer, and THAT
ARGUMENT IS ALWAYS AVAILABLE TO SOMEONE IN A HURRY. A fixed number cannot be
negotiated at the moment it is inconvenient, which is the only moment it
matters. Raise it for everything or not at all.
⛔ DO NOT COPY A SPREAD FROM THE RECORD INTO observedSpread. A figure from
another build on another day standing in for a fresh measurement is a stored
baseline passing as a control — already on this project's list of binding
faults. If you cannot observe the spread, LEAVE THE ENTRY UNPROVEN and say so.
"blindSpots" is what the script does NOT watch, taken from its own declared
scope. run.mjs prints these after a proven script's verdict, because a
proven instrument is still a narrow one.

proven.injected: NO INJECTION NEEDED — the honest production run goes RED on today's build, 7/8 runs, exit 1. Two further falsifications confirmed it fails the right way: the crop moved to empty sky (y=200) reported 'NO REVEAL FOUND' on all 8 rather than a misleading 0ms, and a run below the floor reported 'NO FREEZE FOUND — a finding ABOUT THIS INSTRUMENT'. Reveal window measured 1280–1320ms against the declared 1300ms, 8/8.

emptyInput.pointedAt: The measurement crop moved to empty sky at y=200 — a region of the page where no reveal happens by construction, so any reveal reported there is the instrument talking to itself.
emptyInput.reported: NO REVEAL FOUND — on all 8 runs.
emptyInput.whyItQualifies: It reported an ABSENCE, not a zero. Had it printed '0ms' from the empty crop it would have been character-for-character identical to a clean run on a real crop, and every future 0ms from this harness would have been unfalsifiable. This is the worked example the requirement is written from.

stability.subject: varies
stability.why: The subject is the Q5 reveal freeze — a GPU-side presentation stall that moves run to run on ONE build in ONE session with nothing changed. The script films N runs (default 5) and reveal-stall-measure.mjs reports per-run, median, range and spread.
stability.⚠ observedSpreadIsNull: MEASURED 2026-08-19 AND DELIBERATELY LEFT NULL. 5 films on build 2026-08-19T21-37-45 (production, :3100) reported 0ms on ALL FIVE runs — range 0-0ms, spread 0ms. ⛔ THAT IS NOT A SPREAD OF ZERO, IT IS A NON-MEASUREMENT: reveal-stall-measure.mjs prints 'NO FREEZE FOUND — and that is a finding ABOUT THIS INSTRUMENT' and exits 1, because the stall is live and filmed and a clean verdict means the band, the tolerance or the window is wrong. Recording 0-0ms here would be the quiet zero this file's second requirement exists to prevent — a value that reads as a characterised distribution when nothing was characterised. ⚠ DO NOT copy 40-640ms from the record either: that is a different build on a different day. The entry stays UNPROVEN until a run actually resolves the freeze.
stability.recordOfTheAttempt: The reveal window resolved correctly on all 5 runs (1240-1280ms against the declared 1300ms), so the films are good and the reveal was found — it is the FREEZE the measure pass did not resolve.

proven.whyItCounts: Version 3 of the window anchored on the last frame below 25% of settled brightness — an anchor that excluded the thing it measured. ⚠ WITHOUT THE REQUIRED RED ON TODAY'S BUILD IT WOULD HAVE SHIPPED AS 'THE STALL IS FIXED'. The red was the only thing that caught it.
blindSpots: Desktop 1440x900 only. Mobile is unexercised — a coverage gap, not a timing one.
Q5 only — the reveal after Begin. Not Q4–Q1, not the corridor step.
⚠ 40ms QUANTISATION. 25fps is a FLOOR on resolution: a freeze shorter than 40ms is invisible here, and every duration is bounded, not exact.
NO ATTRIBUTION. It says a freeze happened, where, and for how long. It says NOTHING about why — diagnosis is out of scope.

_demoted.reason: NO EMPTY-INPUT CONTROL ON RECORD. Its red run is genuine and still stands — a width-scoped defect at app/globals.css:1940 took mobile 390x844 RED at 105.58px drift while desktop 1440x900 stayed GREEN at 0px, so the harness DISCRIMINATED rather than merely reacting. But every arm of that proof measured a REAL element. The script was never pointed at nothing, so nothing shows what it says when there is nothing to see.
_demoted.⚠ notInventedOnPurpose: A control was NOT manufactured to keep this entry, and the requirement was NOT weakened to fit it. Demotion is the honest result: the proven list goes 2 → 1.
_demoted.howToRestore: The capability is already there — extras-hold-position.mjs:181 prints '⚠⚠ NOTHING RESOLVED ... A pass here would be VACUOUS — treating it as a failure.' ⚠ BUT A CAPABILITY IS NOT A RUN, which is the rule this file already applies to falsify flags. Point it at a page with no `.enquiry-phrase-extras` (or a selector that matches nothing), confirm it reports the absence rather than a 0px drift, write the run up in project-intelligence/, and move this entry back into "proven" with an emptyInput block.
